text:
kevin: Hi everyone, started today. macbook M1, macOS Ventura. WireGuard connected but can't resolve internal hostnames like corp-api.redwood.local from Terminal (curl gives NXDOMAIN). Browser works fine. Any macOS-specific resolver tricks?
it-support: Welcome Kevin! macOS uses a per-interface DNS resolver system; split-tunnel VPNs often push DNS for the private domain but it doesn't always get wired into the system resolver for apps launched before connect.
kevin: I restarted but still same. Terminal DNS failing while Safari works. Also `dig corp-api.redwood.local` from terminal returns no answer.
alexa: Two quick checks: 1) `scutil --dns` to see what resolver is configured for that domain. 2) Check /etc/resolver/ for a file like `redwood.local` that points to the VPN DNS.
alexa: Example check:```bash
scutil --dns | sed -n '/resolver #/,$p' | sed -n '1,120p'
ls -la /etc/resolver
cat /etc/resolver/redwood.local
```
ops: If `/etc/resolver/redwood.local` is missing, we usually create one via a small script the VPN team deploys. Contents look like:
```text
nameserver 10.240.1.2
search_order 1
```
ops: You can create it manually (sudo) if your laptop is corporate-managed.
kevin: I ran scutil --dns and I see a resolver for 10.240.1.2 but the domain is not listed, scutil lists a different search domain.
it-support: Try flushing the DNS cache after connect: `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache && sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder`. Then retry dig/curl.
kevin: Done, still NXDOMAIN. I also tried `sudo mkdir -p /etc/resolver` and added the file pointing to 10.240.1.2, then `scutil --dns` shows the resolver, but curl still hits NXDOMAIN.
alexa: Are you using Homebrew's `dnsmasq` or any local resolver like `cloudflared`? Those wrap /etc/resolver and can cause conflicts.
kevin: I do have cloudflared running (tunnel to 1.1.1.1) for dev stuff. Should I stop it?
it-support: Yes, try stopping cloudflared temporarily: `brew services stop cloudflared` or `pkill cloudflared`. Then repeat the DNS flush. If that fixes it, we can add an exception for the redwood.local domain.
kevin: Stopping cloudflared fixed it! dig returns A records now and curl works. Thanks.
kevin: Quick follow-up: I still can't `docker pull` the private registry (registry.redwood.internal:5000). Error: TLS handshake timeout. Browser can access the registry UI.
ops: Docker for Mac sometimes routes through its own internal networking stack. Make sure Docker Desktop has the VPN adapter allowed: Settings > Resources > Network > 'Enable VPN Compatibility' (or similar). Also add the registry hostname to Docker's insecure registries if using self-signed certs.
kevin: Docker setting was already enabled. The registry uses our internal CA. How do I add that CA to Docker's trust store?
alexa: Put the CA cert in `~/Library/Group Containers/group.com.docker/pki/ca.pem` or on newer Docker versions, add the CA to the macOS System keychain (login/System) and mark as trusted for SSL. Then restart Docker Desktop.
kevin: Copied CA to System keychain, trusted it, restarted Docker, `docker pull` works. :tada:
infra-bot: Internal docs: https://confluence.redwood/infra/macos-dns-vpn-guide and https://confluence.redwood/infra/docker-mac-registry-setup :thumbsup:
kevin: Thanks all! I'll add a short note in #new-hires summarizing these two fixes for other Mac people (cloudflared conflict + system CA for Docker).
ops: Nice, if you paste the resolver output (redact IPs) we can add a snippet to the onboarding checklist.
kevin: Will do later today. Appreciate the fast help.
